accepted.s: The city of Hyderabad was planned by which official?
accepted.x: Peshwa Mir Momin Astarabadi planned Hyderabad after its foundation by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
accepted.tq: Use the official–institution or official–project association.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the early names associated with Hyderabad and Golconda:
1. Hyderabad was originally known as Bhagyanagar.
2. Golconda was also known by the name Mankal.
3. Mangalavaram is another name associated with old Golconda.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Bhagyanagar is identified as the original name of Hyderabad, while Mankal and Mangalavaram are names associated with old Golconda.
accepted.tq: Combine closely related alternative names and test all listed associations.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The name Bhagyanagar is associated in the tradition mentioned with which person?
o: Mumtaz Mahal, wife of Shah Jahan
Bhagirathi, a Hindu consort associated with Ibrahim
Chand Sultana, wife of Ibrahim Adil Shah II
Saraswati, the muse invoked by Ibrahim Adil Shah II
accepted.x: The name Bhagyanagar is linked in one tradition to Bhagirathi, described as a Hindu consort associated with Ibrahim. Another popular legend associates it with Bhagmati and Muhammad Quli.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a named person linked to a place-name from nearby historical personalities.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which statement best reflects the differing traditions concerning the name Bhagyanagar?
1. One account names Bhagirathi as the consort of Ibrahim.
2. A common legend names Bhagmati in association with Muhammad Quli.
3. Both traditions uniformly identify the same person as the source of the name.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: The two traditions identify different persons: Bhagirathi in one account and Bhagmati in the common legend. Therefore, statement 3 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Spot the false statement that incorrectly merges two confusable traditions.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The foundation stone of the Charminar was laid in which year?
accepted.x: The Charminar was founded in 1591; the foundation stone is specifically associated with 8 February 1591.
accepted.tq: Retain the exact year attached to a monument’s foundation.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Charminar was built with which associated architectural feature?
accepted.x: The Charminar is associated with the four Char Kaman gateways. The other features belong to other monuments or architectural styles mentioned separately.
accepted.tq: Match a monument with its distinctive architectural component.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Mecca Masjid — Begun by Muhammad Qutb Shah
2. Charminar — Founded by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
3. Hussain Sagar — Built by Hussain Shah Wali
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Mecca Masjid was begun by Muhammad Qutb Shah, the Charminar was founded by Muhammad Quli, and Hussain Sagar was built by Hussain Shah Wali.
accepted.tq: Verify each monument–builder pair before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the construction of the Mecca Masjid?
o: It was begun in 1591 and completed in 1614 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
It was begun in 1614 by Muhammad Qutb Shah and completed by Aurangzeb in 1692–93.
It was begun by Aurangzeb in 1692 and completed by Muhammad Qutb Shah.
It was built in 1562 by Hussain Shah Wali.
accepted.x: Muhammad Qutb Shah began the Mecca Masjid in 1614, and Aurangzeb completed it in 1692–93.
accepted.tq: Separate the initiator, successor and completion date in a long construction history.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Jean-Baptiste Tavernier observed approximately how many workers engaged in the construction of the Mecca Masjid?
accepted.x: Tavernier is recorded as having seen about 4,000 workers engaged in the construction of the Mecca Masjid.
accepted.tq: Test an exact numerical observation rather than a general description.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who wrote Dakhni or Urdu poetry under the pen name “Maani”?
accepted.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah wrote Dakhni or Urdu poetry under the pen name Maani and is associated with the Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah.
accepted.tq: Use the author–pen name–work relationship to avoid ruler confusion.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah — Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah
Ibrahim Adil Shah II — Six Travels
accepted.x: Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah is associated with Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. Kitab-i-Nauras was written by Ibrahim Adil Shah II, while Six Travels was written by Tavernier.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between authors and works by using the sure author–title pair.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Urdu is stated to have reached its peak under which Qutb Shahi ruler?
accepted.x: Urdu is stated to have reached its peak under Abdullah Qutb Shah. Ibrahim is separately associated with the title “Chaucer of Urdu.”
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ruler associated with literary prominence from other Qutb Shahi rulers.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ibrahim Qutb Shah is referred to in the literary context as the:
accepted.x: Ibrahim Qutb Shah is referred to as the “Chaucer of Urdu” in the stated literary tradition.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact sobriquet rather than substituting a more familiar literary title.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about monuments associated with Hyderabad:
1. Golconda Fort was the Qutb Shahi capital from the time of Sultan Quli.
2. Ibrahim Qutb Shah built the high walls of Golconda Fort.
3. Hussain Sagar was built in 1562 during Ibrahim’s reign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Golconda served as the Qutb Shahi capital from Sultan Quli, Ibrahim built its high walls, and Hussain Sagar was built by Hussain Shah Wali in 1562 during Ibrahim’s reign.
accepted.tq: Check ruler, monument and date together instead of treating them as isolated facts.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following features is associated with Golconda Fort?
o: Acoustics by which a handclap at the gate could carry to Bala Hisar
A whispering gallery inside the dome
A four-gateway plan called Char Kaman
A square tomb base with onion domes
accepted.x: Golconda Fort was famous for its acoustics, including the transmission of a handclap from the gate to Bala Hisar, and also had piped water.
accepted.tq: Identify the monument from its distinctive functional feature.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Qutb Shahi tombs at Ibrahim Bagh are noted for:
o: Onion domes on square bases and charbagh gardens
Three-arched facades and bulbous domes only
Four Char Kaman gateways surrounding a central minaret
A single massive dome with a whispering gallery
accepted.x: The Qutb Shahi tombs at Ibrahim Bagh are characterised by onion domes on square bases and charbagh gardens.
accepted.tq: Match an architectural description with the correct monument group.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Hussain Sagar was built in 1562 by:
accepted.x: Hussain Sagar was built by Hussain Shah Wali in 1562, during the reign of Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
accepted.tq: Pair the exact year with the builder of the public work.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad - founder, original name, Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Dakhni poetry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Jean-Baptiste Tavernier was a:
1. French jeweller and diamond merchant.
2. Visitor to the Andhra mines in the seventeenth century.
3. Author of Six Travels.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Tavernier was a French jeweller and diamond merchant who visited the Andhra mines in the seventeenth century and wrote Six Travels.
accepted.tq: Test a traveller through profession, period, visit and work together.
accepted.sec: Golconda diamonds and Machilipatnam trade - Tavernier, Kollur mines, European factories  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Tavernier visited the Andhra diamond mines during the reign of:
accepted.x: Tavernier visited the mines during the reign of Abdullah Qutb Shah.
accepted.tq: Apply the traveller–ruler association while avoiding a neighbouring ruler trap.
accepted.sec: Golconda diamonds and Machilipatnam trade - Tavernier, Kollur mines, European factories  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kohinoor diamond was recorded as having come from the:
accepted.x: Tavernier recorded that the Kohinoor came from the Kollur mines, located in the Guntur district on the Krishna.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the famous mine from other nearby diamond-mining centres.
accepted.sec: Golconda diamonds and Machilipatnam trade - Tavernier, Kollur mines, European factories  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kohinoor is stated to have been found in 1656 and presented to Shah Jahan by:
accepted.x: The Kohinoor is stated to have been found in 1656 in the Kollur mines, after which Mir Jumla presented it to Shah Jahan. It is now associated with the British Crown.
accepted.tq: Combine a precise year with the person responsible for a documented transfer.
accepted.sec: Golconda diamonds and Machilipatnam trade - Tavernier, Kollur mines, European factories  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with a diamond-mining centre?
1. Kollur — Guntur district
2. Paritala — Krishna district
3. Ramallakota — Kurnool district
4. Vajrakarur — Anantapur district
accepted.x: The pair Kollur–Guntur is correctly matched; therefore none of the four displayed pairs is incorrect. The question’s NOT premise has no false pair among the options, so the appropriate answer is that all listed pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Check every location pair carefully before accepting a NOT question.
accepted.sec: Golconda diamonds and Machilipatnam trade - Tavernier, Kollur mines, European factories  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At which places were diamonds traded and polished respectively in the Golconda region?
accepted.x: Diamonds were traded at Moti Darwaza and polished at Karwan.
accepted.tq: Separate the marketplace from the place of processing in a paired-location question.
accepted.sec: Golconda diamonds and Machilipatnam trade - Tavernier, Kollur mines, European factories  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs concerning European factories at Machilipatnam:
1. Dutch — 1605
2. English — 1611
3. Captain Hippon — Ship Globe
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Dutch factory dates to 1605, the English factory to 1611, and Captain Hippon arrived in the ship Globe. All three pairs are correct.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure company–year pair and verify the associated agent and vessel.
accepted.sec: Golconda diamonds and Machilipatnam trade - Tavernier, Kollur mines, European factories  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The English obtained permission to establish their presence at Machilipatnam from:
accepted.x: The English came to Machilipatnam with the permission of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. The attribution to Ibrahim Qutb Shah is chronologically inconsistent because he died in 1580.
accepted.tq: Use chronology to reject a ruler who could not have granted the permission.
accepted.sec: Golconda diamonds and Machilipatnam trade - Tavernier, Kollur mines, European factories  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Machilipatnam was particularly famous for the manufacture and trade of:
accepted.x: Machilipatnam was famed for muslin and Kalamkari, in addition to its importance as a trading centre.
accepted.tq: Identify the characteristic goods associated with a historic port.
accepted.sec: Golconda diamonds and Machilipatnam trade - Tavernier, Kollur mines, European factories  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following travellers, apart from Tavernier, described Golconda?
1. Thevenot
2. Bernier
3. Manucci
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Thevenot, Bernier and Manucci also described Golconda. Thevenot’s account is associated with 1666–67.
accepted.tq: Test a complete named list by checking all members rather than one familiar name.
accepted.sec: Golconda diamonds and Machilipatnam trade - Tavernier, Kollur mines, European factories  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Dynasty)
a. Adil Shahi
b. Nizam Shahi
c. Imad Shahi
d. Barid Shahi

List-II (Capital)
i. Bidar
ii. Berar
iii. Bijapur
iv. Ahmadnagar

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Adil Shahi was centred at Bijapur, Nizam Shahi at Ahmadnagar, Imad Shahi at Berar and Barid Shahi at Bidar.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure dynasty–capital pairs and eliminate codes.
accepted.sec: Deccan Sultanates → dynasty + capital + founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Dynasty)
a. Adil Shahi
b. Nizam Shahi
c. Imad Shahi
d. Qutb Shahi

List-II (Founder)
i. Sultan Quli
ii. Malik Ahmad
iii. Yusuf Adil Shah
iv. Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Yusuf Adil Shah founded the Adil Shahi dynasty, Malik Ahmad the Nizam Shahi, Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk the Imad Shahi, and Sultan Quli the Qutb Shahi dynasty.
accepted.tq: Match founders to dynasties, using the distinctive Sultan Quli association as an anchor.
accepted.sec: Deccan Sultanates → dynasty + capital + founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Deccan Sultanates is correct?
o: Berar was founded by the Imad Shahis in 1490.
Golconda was founded by the Adil Shahis in 1489.
Bidar was founded by the Nizam Shahis in 1490.
Bijapur was founded by the Qutb Shahis in 1518.
accepted.x: Berar was the capital of the Imad Shahi dynasty, founded by Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk in 1490.
accepted.tq: Use the capital–dynasty–founder–year chain to detect swapped rulers.
accepted.sec: Deccan Sultanates → dynasty + capital + founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Deccan Sultanates according to the year of their foundation, from earliest to latest:
A. Adil Shahi
B. Nizam Shahi
C. Imad Shahi
D. Qutb Shahi
accepted.x: The correct order is Adil Shahi (1489), Nizam Shahi (1490), Imad Shahi (1490), and Qutb Shahi (1518).
accepted.tq: Arrange dynasties by their foundation years, noting the two successive 1490 foundations.
accepted.sec: Deccan Sultanates → dynasty + capital + founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
1. Adil Shahi — Ended by Aurangzeb in 1686
2. Nizam Shahi — Ended by Shah Jahan in 1633
3. Imad Shahi — Ended by Ahmadnagar in 1574
4. Qutb Shahi — Ended by Shah Jahan in 1633
accepted.x: The Qutb Shahi dynasty ended under Aurangzeb in 1687, not under Shah Jahan in 1633. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped conqueror and end-date in a dynasty table.
accepted.sec: Deccan Sultanates → dynasty + capital + founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Barid Shahi dynasty of Bidar was associated with which founders?
o: Qasim Barid and Amir Ali Barid
Yusuf Adil Shah and Malik Ahmad
Muhammad Quli and Abdullah Qutb Shah
accepted.x: The Barid Shahi dynasty of Bidar is associated with Qasim Barid and Amir Ali Barid.
accepted.tq: Recall the two-person founder association in a dynasty with more than one named founder.
accepted.sec: Deccan Sultanates → dynasty + capital + founder  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ibrahim Adil Shah II wrote which work in Dakhni?
accepted.x: Ibrahim Adil Shah II wrote Kitab-i-Nauras in Dakhni and invoked Saraswati as his muse.
accepted.tq: Match the ruler-author with the exact literary work.
accepted.sec: Bijapur - Ibrahim Adil Shah II, Kitab-i-Nauras, Gol Gumbaz  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Ibrahim Adil Shah II:
1. He wrote Kitab-i-Nauras in Dakhni.
2. He invoked Saraswati as his muse.
3. Firishta dedicated Tarikh-i-Firishta to him.
4. He married Chand Sultana, the sister of Muhammad Quli.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Ibrahim Adil Shah II was a Dakhni author, invoked Saraswati, received Firishta’s dedication, and married Chand Sultana, Muhammad Quli’s sister.
accepted.tq: Test several biographical details in a single coded combination.
accepted.sec: Bijapur - Ibrahim Adil Shah II, Kitab-i-Nauras, Gol Gumbaz  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which work of Firishta was dedicated to Ibrahim Adil Shah II?
accepted.x: Firishta dedicated Tarikh-i-Firishta, also called Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi, to Ibrahim Adil Shah II.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the author’s work from works written by or describing other rulers.
accepted.sec: Bijapur - Ibrahim Adil Shah II, Kitab-i-Nauras, Gol Gumbaz  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which monument is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah?
accepted.x: Gol Gumbaz is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah. Ibrahim Rauza is the tomb associated with Ibrahim Adil Shah II.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ruler commemorated by two nearby Bijapur monuments.
accepted.sec: Bijapur - Ibrahim Adil Shah II, Kitab-i-Nauras, Gol Gumbaz  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Gol Gumbaz is correct?
1. It is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah.
2. It has a whispering gallery.
3. It is among the world’s largest domes.
4. There are arches and structures around it.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe Gol Gumbaz. It is not an isolated dome without surrounding arches and structures.
accepted.tq: Reject an absolute architectural claim by checking the complete monument description.
accepted.sec: Bijapur - Ibrahim Adil Shah II, Kitab-i-Nauras, Gol Gumbaz  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following features is characteristic of the Bijapur style mentioned?
o: Three-arched facades, bulbous domes and cornices
Four Char Kaman gateways and a plague memorial
A handclap acoustic system leading to Bala Hisar
Charbagh gardens and onion domes on square bases only
accepted.x: The Bijapur style is associated with three-arched facades, bulbous domes and cornices. The other options describe features associated with different monuments.
accepted.tq: Compare architectural styles by isolating the feature set belonging to Bijapur.
accepted.sec: Bijapur - Ibrahim Adil Shah II, Kitab-i-Nauras, Gol Gumbaz  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Malik-e-Maidan is associated with:
o: The Qutb Shahi tombs at Ibrahim Bagh
accepted.x: Malik-e-Maidan is a notable cannon associated with the Bijapur tradition.
accepted.tq: Identify the object from its historical and regional association.
